extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (schools, colleges, universities), Title IX coordinators, campus administrators, and institutional legal counsel responsible for Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements from the Department of Education's Title IX final regulations governing reporting, supportive measures, grievance procedures, evidence handling, remedies, informal resolution, timeframes, and protections (e.g., retaliation, presumption of non-responsibility) in response to alleged sexual harassment in education programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies may be punitive or disciplinary
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations revise §106.45(b)(1)(i) to expressly state that remedies, unlike supportive measures, may be punitive or disciplinary and need not avoid burdening the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction exists because remedies are required after a respondent has been determined responsible under a grievance process that complies with §106.45. Remedies can include individualized services similar to supportive measures but may also discipline or burden the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any person may report sexual harassment at any time
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8(a) states that any person may report sexual harassment (whether or not the reporter is the alleged victim) using the contact information listed for the Title IX Coordinator, and that such a report may be made “at any time (including during non-business hours)” via telephone, email, or mail to the office address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must list contact information for the Title IX Coordinator and prominently display it on their websites so reports can be made through those means; a report to the Title IX Coordinator can constitute 'notice' for purposes of 'actual knowledge' (§106.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge and prompt response obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.30 defines 'actual knowledge' to include notice (such as a report to the Title IX Coordinator); §106.44(a) requires a prompt response to actual knowledge of sexual harassment in a recipient's program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A report to the Title IX Coordinator imposes on the recipient the duty to respond promptly; see related discussions of the scope of 'education program or activity' and promptness requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator discretion to sign formal complaints while protecting complainant participation rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations at §106.30 (defining 'formal complaint') give Title IX Coordinators discretion to sign a formal complaint even where the complainant does not wish to participate, while protecting every complainant's right not to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.71 prohibits retaliation against any person exercising rights under Title IX, including participation or refusal to participate in any grievance process. Coordinators may initiate complaints but must respect complainant choices and protect against retaliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to be assisted by an advisor of choice
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(5)(iv) gives both parties equal opportunity to be assisted by an advisor of choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are required to provide both parties the same opportunity to select an advisor; supportive measures and advisor access recognize that grievance participation can be stressful for both complainants and respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sexual harassment and intent requirement for certain sex offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.30 defining 'sexual harassment' does not impose an independent intent or mens rea requirement on conduct that constitutes sexual harassment; however, the sexual offense of 'fondling' (included under 'sexual assault') includes an element of touching 'for the purpose of sexual gratification.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should take care to apply that intent requirement to incidents of alleged fondling so that, for example, unwanted touching committed by young children—with no sexualized intent—is distinguished from Title IX sexual harassment and can be addressed outside these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation prohibition interpreted consistent with constitutional rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department emphasizes the purpose of §106.6(d) in new §106.71(b) (prohibiting retaliation) to remind recipients that in deciding if conduct constitutes retaliation, the Department will interpret the prohibition in a manner consistent with constitutional rights such as First Amendment rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should assess alleged retaliation with attention to protected constitutional activities and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department will not second-guess recipients' disciplinary decisions; focus on remedies implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: While the Department requires recipients to effectively implement remedies for a complainant when a recipient finds a respondent responsible, it will not second-guess the recipient's determination of responsibility solely because the Department would have weighed the evidence differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy reflects deference to recipients' disciplinary judgments in the administrative enforcement process; the Department's enforcement focuses on whether recipients complied with procedural and remedial obligations under the regulations (see §§106.45(b)(1)(i), 106.45(b)(7)(iv), 106.44(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process must comply with §106.45 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of addressing formal complaints of sexual harassment, a recipient's grievance process must comply with the requirements of §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble provides detailed subsections (e.g., summary of §106.45, role of due process) that explain §106.45's procedural protections and requirements which recipients must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of formal complaints when arising from same facts
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(4) gives recipients discretion to consolidate formal complaints involving multiple parties where the allegations arise from the same facts or circumstances; in consolidated matters, the grievance process applies to more than one complainant and/or more than one respondent, but each party is still an 'individual' and not a group or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may consolidate for efficiency when facts overlap, but must treat each party individually within the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution limited and voluntary
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(9) gives recipients discretion to offer and facilitate informal resolution processes, such as mediation or restorative justice, subject to each party voluntarily agreeing after giving informed, written consent; informal resolution may only be offered after a formal complaint has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal resolution may not be required, cannot be conditioned on enrollment/employment/rights, and may never be offered to resolve allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student. Recipients must notify parties about ramifications before obtaining consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in procedural mechanics (time frames, virtual hearings, evidence platforms, standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may decide whether to calculate time frames using calendar days, school days, or other methods; §106.45(b)(6)(i) allows, but does not require, live hearings to be held virtually; §106.45(b)(5)(vi) removes the requirement that evidence be provided via a file-sharing platform; §106.45(b)(7)(i) removes a limitation tying the preponderance standard to non-sexual conduct policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations permit recipients flexibility in logistics and technology subject to the substantive requirements (e.g., objective evaluation, evidence access).

rubrics_metrics.name: No adverse inference from a party's failure to appear or answer cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(6)(i) provides that the decision-maker cannot draw any inference about responsibility or non-responsibility solely based on a party's failure to appear or answer cross-examination questions at a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protection applies in contexts such as when a respondent is concurrently facing criminal charges and chooses not to appear to avoid self-incrimination; recipients must avoid penalizing non-appearance with an automatic adverse inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence (inculpatory and exculpatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to §106.45 requirements, a grievance process must provide for objective evaluation of all relevant evidence, both inculpatory and exculpatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence considered must be directly related to the allegations under investigation; recipients must ensure balanced and objective assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of law enforcement evidence and limits of police reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations precludes a recipient from using evidence obtained from law enforcement in a §106.45 grievance process; however, police investigations or reports may be useful for fact gathering but are not determinative of whether harassment occurred under Title IX and do not relieve the school of its duty to respond promptly and effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may incorporate law enforcement information but must apply Title IX standards independently because criminal legal standards differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures with or without a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations mandate that recipients offer supportive measures to complainants with or without a formal complaint so complainants receive meaningful assistance in restoring or preserving equal access to education even when a matter does not result in an investigation and adjudication under §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are defined in §106.30; these measures are distinct from remedies and are intended to assist complainants promptly regardless of formal grievance status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures may be offered to respondents as well
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department recognizes that the grievance process may be difficult and stressful for both parties; supportive measures may be offered to complainants and respondents, and §106.45(b)(5)(iv) requires recipients to provide both parties the same opportunity to select an advisor of choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should consider supports for both parties where appropriate to ensure fairness and access to the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of non-responsibility explained and limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumption of non-responsibility does not permit recipients automatically or prematurely to 'believe respondents' or 'disbelieve complainants.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption requires that respondents be treated as not responsible at the outset, but does not dictate automatic credibility assignments for either party; see discussion in §106.45(b)(1)(iv) subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably prompt time frame and permissible extensions for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(v) provides that the recipient's designated reasonably prompt time frame for completion of a grievance process is subject to temporary delay or limited extension for good cause, which may include concurrent law enforcement activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must set and follow reasonably prompt time frames but may pause or extend for legitimate reasons like investigations by law enforcement; such delays should be documented and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence disclosure requirements — directly related evidence and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to §106.45 requirements, evidence sent to the parties for inspection and review must be directly related to the allegations under investigation; such evidence may have been gathered by the recipient 'from a party or other source' including law enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure parties receive all evidence directly related to allegations, while balancing privacy and relevance; the process must permit meaningful inspection and review prior to adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent display of Title IX Coordinator contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8 requires that contact information for the Title IX Coordinator be listed and prominently displayed on recipients' websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making contact information conspicuous facilitates reporting and constitutes part of the recipient's obligation to provide notice and access to reporting mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate indifference standard adopted and tailored
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations adopt the Supreme Court's deliberate indifference liability standard but tailor that standard to achieve policy aims of administrative enforcement of Title IX's non-discrimination mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the 'Deliberate Indifference' subsection for discussion of how the standard is applied in administrative enforcement contexts; the approach departs from earlier guidance while still aiming to effectuate statutory non-discrimination objectives.
